title: Uniformly bounded algebraic coordinates in a countable-dimensional ultrametric space
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with its extended nonarchimedean norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V\ne0$ be an $E$-vector space with a norm satisfying $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$ and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$, with $\|v\|=0$ precisely for $v=0$. Suppose $V$ is spanned algebraically by a finite or countable sequence; no completeness of $V$ is assumed. For any prescribed $v_0\ne0$ there is an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ (every vector has a unique finite linear expansion) with $0\in J$, $b_0=v_0$, where $J$ is either $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ for some $d\geq1$ or $\mathbf N$, and constants $0<c\leq C<\infty$ such that for every finitely supported family $(a_j)$ in $E$,
$$c\max_j|a_j|\leq\Big\|\sum_ja_jb_j\Big\|\leq C\max_j|a_j|.$$
The maximum of the empty support is zero. In particular every coordinate projection, every projection onto an arbitrary subset of $J$, and every linear map sending the basis bijectively onto a subset of itself are continuous. The inverse from that coordinate subspace onto $V$ is continuous when the subset is in bijection with $J$. These are algebraic finite-support coordinates, not an assertion about infinite series.

proof.text: Prepend the prescribed vector to the spanning sequence. Recursively append the residual obtained by subtracting a nearest point in the span of the previous finite tuple, using [lem-sfb-finite-ultrametric-best-approximation]. Keep zero residuals temporarily. For u in the previous span and any scalar a, minimality applied to w-a^{-1}u gives ||a(x-w)|| <= ||u+a(x-w)|| when a is nonzero; a=0 is immediate. Applying ultrametricity to u=(u+a(x-w))-a(x-w) then proves ||u+a(x-w)||=max(||u||,|a| ||x-w||). The private residual_orthogonal lemma proves this directly, without the separately stated orthogonal-extension theorem. Induction gives the exact weighted maximum formula for every finite prefix. The nearest point lies in the previous span and s_n is the sum of its residual and nearest point, so the residual sequence spans every original generator. The first residual is v_0 since the initial span is zero.

proof.text: Extend the prefix formula to arbitrary finite supports by zero padding. Restrict to the subset I of natural indices with nonzero residuals. This restriction still spans, and the exact weighted maximum formula implies linear independence: if a finite linear combination is zero, each nonnegative term |a_i| ||t_i|| is zero, hence every coefficient is zero. Form its algebraic basis with Module.Basis.mk. Since 0 belongs to I, classify the countable nonempty index type as finite or countably infinite, use an equivalence to Iio d or all naturals, and compose with a transposition to put the prescribed vector at index zero. No completeness or infinite sum is used.

proof.text: Choose any scalar q in E with norm greater than one (NormedField.exists_one_lt_norm). For each basis vector except the first apply Mathlib rescale_to_shell with epsilon=||q||, obtaining a nonzero scalar d_j such that 1 <= ||d_j b_j|| < ||q||. Take d_0=1 and use Module.Basis.unitsSMul. Substitution of a_j d_j in the old orthogonality formula preserves the weighted maximum formula. Set c=min(||v_0||,1) and C=max(||v_0||,||q||). Every basis vector has norm in [c,C], c>0, and the weighted formula gives the asserted two bounds, with the empty support handled separately. This uses generic nontrivial normed-field rescaling rather than any special uniformizer construction.

proof.text: From the lower bound each coefficient satisfies |a_j| <= c^{-1}||v||. Ultrametricity bounds a finite sum of images of basis vectors by C times the largest coefficient whenever those images have norm at most C. Thus subset projections and injective basis relabelings have operator bound C/c and are continuous by LinearMap.mkContinuous. For a basis injection sigma, the coefficient family of the image is Finsupp.embDomain sigma of the original family, so its maximum dominates the original maximum. The lower image bound and upper domain bound give ||v|| <= (C/c)||f(v)||. ContinuousLinearMap.isUniformEmbedding_of_bound proves the final embedding clause, including continuity of the inverse onto the range.

lean.statement: theorem exists_countable_ultrametric_basis (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (V : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup V] (h_ultra : ∀ x y : V, ‖x + y‖ ≤ max ‖x‖ ‖y‖) (v₀ : V) (hv₀ : v₀ ≠ 0) : letI := spectralNorm.nontriviallyNormedField (Padic l) E ∀ [NormedSpace E V], (∃ s : ℕ → V, Submodule.span E (Set.range s) = ⊤) → ∃ (J : Set ℕ) (h₀ : 0 ∈ J) (b : Module.Basis J E V) (c C : ℝ), (J = Set.univ ∨ ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ J = Set.Iio d) ∧ b ⟨0, h₀⟩ = v₀ ∧ 0 < c ∧ c ≤ C ∧ (∀ a : J →₀ E, c * ((a.support.sup (fun j ↦ ‖a j‖₊) : NNReal) : ℝ) ≤ ‖b.repr.symm a‖ ∧ ‖b.repr.symm a‖ ≤ C * ((a.support.sup (fun j ↦ ‖a j‖₊) : NNReal) : ℝ)) ∧ (∀ j : J, Continuous (b.coord j)) ∧ (∀ S : Set J, Continuous (b.constr E (fun j ↦ if j ∈ S then b j else 0))) ∧ (∀ σ : J ↪ J, Topology.IsEmbedding (b.constr E (fun j ↦ b (σ j))))
